topic: How does a lithium-ion battery actually charge?
title: How Does A Lithium-Ion Battery Actually Charge?
false_sentence: When empty, most positively charged lithium ions are sitting over on the positive cathode side.
correct_version: In a discharged lithium-ion battery, most lithium ions are actually stored within the structure of the cathode, not just sitting on its side. Charging involves these ions de-intercalating from the cathode and moving to the anode.
why: The narration implies ions are sitting loosely in the electrolyte or surface of the cathode when discharged, whereas they are chemically intercalated within the cathode material lattice.
